source: Quiz 4 - Sessions 1-5: Building and Improving Agent Skills
question: Why can a recurrent block perform extra work without adding independent parameters on each pass?

options.text: Extra passes add new layers, each with separately learned weights.
options.feedback: Adding independently parameterized layers would increase the parameter count. A recurrent block instead reuses its existing weights on later passes.

options.text: The extra work comes from fitting more input tokens in the context.
options.feedback: Context capacity and recurrent computation describe different resources. The same block can process internal representations again without a larger input sequence.

options.text: Each pass learns improved weights that replace the previous values.
options.feedback: Recurrent depth here describes inference with trained weights. The numerical representation changes across passes, rather than a new training update replacing the weights.

options.text: The same learned transformation is applied to successive states.
options.feedback: Weight sharing reuses the existing numerical values. More applications can increase computation and latency without increasing the count of independent weights.
